title: MongoDB Multi-Stage Aggregation Pipeline Query Assignment
mechanisms_and_formulas: $match filters documents by status='DELIVERED' and orderDate within 2024
$unwind deconstructs the items array so each element becomes a separate pipeline document
$lookup joins orders with products on items.product_id = products._id
$project removes _id and formats revenue to two decimal places
factual_summary_text: The assignment asks students to build a multi‑stage MongoDB aggregation pipeline that extracts business metrics from an e‑commerce database containing orders, products, and users. The pipeline must begin with a $match stage that selects only orders whose status is DELIVERED and whose orderDate falls within the calendar year 2024. Next, a $unwind stage deconstructs the items array so each product line can be processed individually. A $lookup stage then joins each unwound item to the products collection using items.product_id and the product _id, bringing in category and cost information. The $group stage aggregates by product category, calculating total_revenue as the sum of quantity multiplied by unit_price and average_item_margin as the average of unit_price minus product cost. Results are ordered in descending total_revenue with a $sort stage, and a final $project stage removes the internal _id field and rounds revenue values to two decimal places. The problem also highlights an anti‑pattern: placing $unwind before $match, which would cause unnecessary memory consumption, and stresses the importance of indexing the fields used in the initial $match for optimal pipeline performance.
